recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Foundation — employee + audit
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero external module dependencies. Employee provides identity/manager lookup needed by every other module. Audit is a cross-cutting concern required by GP-002 for all state-changing operations. Both can be built and tested in isolation.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: policy + balance
recommended_phases.rationale: Policy depends on nothing (static rules/config). Balance depends only on employee (for identity validation). Both are prerequisites for leave orchestration. Can be built in parallel.

app_notes: Dependency direction verified: no cycles. All edges flow inward — leave (orchestrator) depends on all other modules; balance and notification depend only on employee; employee, audit, and policy have zero module dependencies. The LeaveService orchestrates the full submit/approve/reject workflow: it calls IPolicyService.validateRequest before submission, IBalanceService.deductBalance on approval (and restoreBalance on rejection/cancellation), INotificationService for manager/employee alerts, and IAuditService.record for every state change per GP-002. Routes layer enforces RBAC (GP-005) and input validation (GP-003). All DB access is through repository interfaces (GP-001). The existing PascalCase module directories (LeaveStatus, LeaveRequest, etc.) are superseded by this design; the lowercase dot-notation convention from the existing status/uptime modules is followed.
